handbook-garments-title: [Arts & Crafts: Tailor] Crafting Mechanic: Tailored garments
handbook-garments-text:
Sewing

Right click a mannequin with a sewing material (cloth: woven cloth, woven linen, vanilla linen or cloth; leather; a cured pelt; hard bits: wood (sticks, planks), metal (metal bits, nuggets) or bone), pick a garment, put one item into each part slot, move the woven patterns under the parts, then cut and sew. Each filled part uses 1 item; optional parts may stay empty and are then left off the garment. Patterns are never stretched: they repeat on large parts and are cut off on small ones.

Garments

Tunic (shirt): body, skirt, sleeves; optional collar.
Vest (over a shirt): body, neck trim; optional buttons.
Pants: waistband, legs; optional suspenders, optional buttons (on the suspenders, or on the waistband without them).
Fur wrap (shoulders): one pelt or leather.
Toga (shirt): drape; optional fibula.
Jeogori (shirt): body, collar band, sleeves; optional goreum tie.
Chima (legs): skirt.
Hood (head): hood; optional shoulder mantle.
Head scarf (head): scarf; optional pearls along its edge.
Scarf mask (face): mask.
Scarf (neck): scarf.
Cape (shoulders): cape; optional collar.
Arm wraps (arms): left and right wrap.
Gloves (hands): right and left glove.
Belt (waist): strap; optional buckle.
Badge (emblem): badge; optional ribbon.
Parka (over a shirt): body, skirt, sleeves, hood; optional fur collar, edging, stitching.
Boots (feet): left and right boot, soles; optional fur ring, stripes, lining.
handbook-sewing-title: [Arts & Crafts: Tailor] Crafting Mechanic: Sewing guide
handbook-sewing-text:
On the mannequin (no window needed)

1. Pick: look at a mannequin and press F (empty hand or a sewing material), or right click its body with nothing started. Choose a body part, then a garment. The mannequin shows it as a faint ghost. Parts with variants (the parka's hem and collar) get a row of buttons for their shape: pick one before or while draping; the part keeps its cloth when you switch (uncut it first).
2. Drape: right click each part with a material it takes (woven cloth, woven linen, vanilla linen or cloth, leather, a cured pelt, or a hard bit: wood, metal, bone). The cloth pattern starts under the crosshair. Right click near a face edge to move it one cell, in the middle to re-anchor it; sneak + right click turns it a quarter.
3. Optional parts (collar, buttons...): sneak + right click their place with an empty hand to switch them on or off; holding a fitting hard bit shows empty button places as ghost.
4. Cut: right click each draped cloth with shears or a knife. Cut cloth is locked in place; sneak + shears uncuts it. Tools lose no durability.
5. Sew: right click the mannequin with a sewing kit once every part is draped and cut. The kit is not used up; only the part materials are (1 item per filled part). The mannequin wears the garment, or you get it when that slot is taken. New garments are in perfect condition.
6. Cancel: sneak + right click the mannequin (not the garment) with shears: materials and charged twine come back.

Sewing window

Right click the mannequin with an empty hand while you sew there (or press "Sewing window" in the garment picker). Tab Sew: body part and garment buttons, one material slot per part, the garment texture flat (drag a cloth part to move its pattern; wheel zooms, middle drag pans), arrows and Rotate for the selected part, the Sleeves toggle, "Cut and sew" and "Cancel". Tab Embroider: see the embroidery guide.

Closing the window (Esc) keeps everything: materials, garment, layout and pending stitches stay on the mannequin. Walk around it and right click to come back. While you sew, others nearby cannot take over; when you leave (32 blocks or log out) another player with a material can.
handbook-embroidery-title: [Arts & Crafts: Tailor] Crafting Mechanic: Embroidery guide
handbook-embroidery-text:
Stitching on the mannequin

Hold twine (dyed or flax) and look at a garment on a mannequin: the garment in progress or a tailored garment it wears. The brush shows in the twine colour. Right click (hold and move to draw) stitches; sneak + right click picks out. F changes the brush (1, 2, 4, 8). Fur, buttons and other hard parts take no stitches.

Pending stitches

New stitches are pending until you apply them: nothing is charged yet, and everyone sees them on the mannequin. Stitches made on the mannequin and in the window are the same pending stitches. They stay when you close the window, switch tabs or log out; only Apply or Discard ends them (and cancelling or switching the garment in progress). A garment with pending stitches cannot be sewn until they are applied or discarded.

Embroider tab of the sewing window

Open it with twine (right click the mannequin off the garment) or with an empty hand while stitches are pending. Pick the garment, a twine you carry and a brush.
Mouse: left click or drag stitches, right click or shift + left picks out. Wheel zooms at the mouse, middle drag or space + left drag pans.
Keys: [ and ] brush size, X pick out on / off, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) redo, + - 0 zoom and fit.
Undo and redo step through whole strokes, from the window and from the mannequin alike. "Discard pending" drops every pending stitch of that garment.

Cost

Apply takes 1 twine per colour that is new on that garment (from your hotbar and backpack). A colour once paid on a garment is free from then on, wherever you stitch it. Picking out is free and never refunds. Cancelling or switching the garment in progress gives the twine charged for it back.

actailor:handbook-loom-text:
Overview

The Flying Shuttle Loom is a floor loom with shafts and treadles that weaves twine into patterned cloth, right on the loom in the world (no crafting menu).

Building it

Craft a Loom Frame (debarked logs, chisel, axe), a Loom Heddle (planks, flax twine) and a Loom Beater (planks, sticks, nails and strips, chisel), then combine the three. The loom is a 3x2x2 multiblock.

How to Use

1. Sit down
Right-click the bench to sit; jump to stand up.

2. Warp
Load each warp thread at the back of the loom with twine.

3. Shuttles
Fill up to 4 shuttles in the shuttle boxes at both ends of the beater.

4. Weave a draft
Press F with an empty hand to open the draft window (see Weaving drafts), then press a treadle on the tie-up board and beat the row in with the reed.

5. Cut
Cut the finished cloth off with shears or a knife. Flax-only cloth gives vanilla linen.

Workflow

1. Harvest fibers (flax, wool, cotton, etc.)
2. Spin fibers into twine using the Spinning Wheel or the Drop Spindle
3. Weave twine into cloth on the loom
4. Use cloth for crafting clothes, bags, and other items

wovenlinen-handbook-uses-text:
Woven linen is what a loom cut gives (a cloth of plain flax twine only gives vanilla linen instead):
• Linen + stick in the crafting grid (like vanilla linen): one dyed colour that vanilla cloth has gives that vanilla cloth (1 per linen); golden twine or several colours give woven cloth with the pattern.
• Like vanilla linen: right click a wall, floor or ceiling (sneaking or not) to place it as a thin patterned panel. Break the panel to get the linen back.

blockdesc-wovencarpet-large-*: A 1x2 carpet, woven on a loom twice as long as a cloth, or made from two woven cloths (top one = far end). It extends away from you; the first woven row lies nearest.

wovencloth-handbook-uses-text:
Woven cloth keeps its pattern wherever it goes (cloths are square: 16 x 16, or 32 x 32 in a world set to double precision):
• Upholstered chair: planks and one woven cloth, like a vanilla chair; the seat shows the middle of the pattern.
• Small carpet: one woven cloth (one linen is worth one small carpet).
• Large carpet (1x2): two woven cloths, one above the other (top = far end). Looms can also weave carpets directly (F picker on an empty loom).
• Tapestry: hold a hammer in one hand and the cloth in the other, then right click a wall: one block per cloth. Break the tapestry to get the cloth back.
• Sneak + right click the ground to lay it down as a pile.

handbook-weavingdraft-title: [Arts & Crafts: Weaver] Crafting Mechanic: Weaving drafts
handbook-weavingdraft-text:
The one idea

Warp threads run along the cloth. They are loaded at the back of the Flying Shuttle Loom before weaving and stay for the whole cloth. Weft is thrown across one row (a pick) at a time from a shuttle, so its colour can change every row.

Each warp thread runs through one of 4 shafts. A treadle lifts some shafts; their threads go up. At every crossing the lifted warp shows its colour, everywhere else the weft shows.

Rule: cell = warp lifted ? warp colour : weft colour. Twill, diamonds, checks and houndstooth all come from this rule; nothing is painted cell by cell.

The draft window

Sit at the loom (or stand by it) with an empty hand and press F. Hover any cell for help.
• Warp colours (top strip): one colour per warp thread; picking one loads that twine (it must be in your inventory).
• Threading (below, shaft 4 on top): the shaft of each thread. Fixed while a cloth is on the warp.
• Tie-up (right of the threading): the shafts each treadle lifts. Click to tie or untie, any time.
• Drawdown (centre, row 1 on top): the cloth that comes out. Rows above the gold line are woven and read-only.
• Treadling and weft (right of the drawdown): the treadle and weft colour of each row.

Editing

• Colour brush All / 8 / 4 / 2 / 1: how many threads or rows a colour click covers (hover shows them). Shift + click a second cell: exactly that range.
• Presets: the small pictures show the threading, tie-up or treadling they set; hover for the name.
• Treadling section: rows from ... to ..., a treadle sequence (e.g. 1 2 3 4), Apply. Clicking a drawdown row sets "from".
• Undo / Redo (buttons, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y): every draft edit, already on the loom. Warp loads are real twine and are not undone.
• Undo last row: unweaves the last woven row (the same as sneak + reed); it becomes editable again.
• Copy square: pick a size (2 / 4 / 8 / 16), press Copy square, click the centre of the square to copy in the drawdown, then click where it goes: threading, treadling, warp and weft colours of those threads and rows are copied (one undo step). Escape or right click cancels.
• New weft colour: a colour no shuttle holds is wound onto a free shuttle (one twine from your inventory); with all 4 shuttles full you are told and the shuttles stay as they are.
• Checks: a treadle that lifts no thread or every thread makes no cloth (the loom will not weave that row); floats longer than 5 cells snag (orange).
• Draft code: Copy / Paste + import share drafts (the same code as the web designer and /actailor draft).

Weaving it

1. Nothing to apply: every edit goes to the loom at once, and anyone at the loom sees it live.
2. Load the warp at the back: twine + right click a thread (the brush sets how many); missing colours show orange in the window.
3. Wind twine on the shuttles at the beater ends (up to 4 colours); the plan picks the shuttle of each row.
4. Each row starts with its treadle pressed (gold on the tie-up board); right click the board to press another.
5. Beat the row in with the reed. Sneak + reed rolls a row back.
6. When all rows are woven, cut the cloth off with a knife or shears; the twine is charged then.

Recipes to try

• Plain weave: Tabby tie-up, treadling 1 2.
• Twill: Straight threading, 2/2 twill tie-up, treadling 1 2 3 4.
• Herringbone: Point threading, 2/2 twill, treadling 1 2 3 4.
• Diamonds: Point threading, 2/2 twill, treadling 1 2 3 4 3 2.
• Houndstooth: Straight threading, 2/2 twill, treadling 1 2 3 4; warp and weft 4 dark, 4 light (colour brush 4).

actailor:handbook-spinningwheel-title: [Arts & Crafts: Weaver] Crafting Mechanic: Spinning Wheel
actailor:handbook-spinningwheel-text:
Overview

The Spinning Wheel is a foot-powered crafting station used to spin raw fibers into twine and thread. It provides a more immersive alternative to crafting twine by hand in the grid.

How to Use

1. Place the spinning wheel
The spinning wheel is a 2x2x2 multiblock structure. Place it on a flat surface with enough clearance.

2. Sit down
Right-click the spinning wheel to sit at it. Your character will take a seat at the wheel, ready to spin.

3. Open the crafting menu
While seated, right click any part to open the spinning wheel interface. This allows you to load fibers and collect your output.

4. Add fibers
Place spinnable fibers (such as Flax Fibers) into the input slot.

5. Spin
Once seated with fibers loaded, your character will automatically begin spinning. The wheel will turn and fibers will be converted into twine over time.

6. Collect output
Remove the finished twine from the output slot when spinning is complete.

Spinnable Materials

Vanilla:
Flax Fibers produce Flax Twine

With Wool and More mod:
Wool Fibers produce Wool Twine

With Floral Zones Caribbean mod:
Cotton Fibers produce Flax Twine

With Pemmican mod:
Papyrus Fibers and Algae produce Flax Twine

Portable Alternative

If you need to spin fibers while traveling, consider using the Drop Spindle. It is slower but can be used anywhere without needing to sit at a station.

Tips

- The spinning wheel works faster than hand-crafting twine in the grid
- You can configure spin times and quantities in the mod settings
- Server admins can restrict the spinning wheel to specific player classes

actailor:handbook-dropspindle-title: [Arts & Crafts: Weaver] Crafting Mechanic: Drop Spindle
actailor:handbook-dropspindle-text:
Overview

The Drop Spindle is a simple, portable tool for spinning fibers into twine while on the move. It is slower than the Spinning Wheel but requires no station or seating.

How to Use

1. Prepare your tools
Place the fibers you want to spin in your offhand.
Hold the Drop Spindle in your main hand.

2. Spin
Hold Right Click to spin the fibers. You will need to do this twice per batch.

3. Extract Twine
Once spinning is complete, Sneak + Right Click to remove the finished twine.

Tips

- The drop spindle works with the same fibers as the Spinning Wheel (flax, cotton, wool, etc.)
- Watch your progress in the chat (if enabled in config) or by the spinning animation
- You can configure whether progress messages appear in the mod settings
- Ideal for travel or when you don't have access to a full spinning wheel
